entities.name: Scadutree Avatar
aliases: Great Guardian of the Shadow Tree

facts.text: Guardians protecting the passage to the deep root depths, and through it Godwyn's resting place, stand between the ordinary world and the aftermath of the Night of the Black Knives, the event in which Godwyn was killed.
The Golden Order built these guardians to ensure that what happened within the roots of the Erdtree stayed hidden there.
The Mimic Tear is encountered in Nokron and is a silver tear, a form of living mercury native to the eternal cities of the Nox.
The Mimic Tear takes on the player character's appearance, weapons, armor, and spells, fighting as an exact copy of the player without their consciousness or history.
Fighting the Mimic Tear is interpreted as a fight against one's own reflection, raising questions about identity and selfhood without the game commenting on it directly.
Rykard's serpent god boss form represents the complete expression of what Rykard became after fully merging with the serpent he devoured, rather than wearing a human face.
A human voice speaks through Rykard's serpent form, indicating that a vestige of Rykard's own consciousness persists and still chooses to act even from within the god-devouring serpent's body.
The Stone Digger Troll, found in the Old Altus Tunnel, and other troll enemies belong to a tradition of giant humanoid beings that predates the Golden Order's specific social organization.
Trolls in Elden Ring function primarily as laborers, valued for their size and strength in mining operations, construction, and heavy infrastructure work.
Trolls' aggression toward the player is interpreted as the defensive response of beings long accustomed to dangerous labor, rather than the behavior of guardians or dedicated enemies.
The Night's Cavalry Leader is the most powerful of the Night's Cavalry, a group encountered only after dark at specific locations.
The Night's Cavalry represent an old knightly tradition that predates the Golden Order's reorganization of martial culture around the Erdtree.
The Night's Cavalry serve the night itself rather than any specific lord or institution, and have patrolled the same routes since before the Shattering.
Demi-Human Queen Gilika and her variants lead groups of Demi-Human enemies and represent one of many peoples of the Lands Between who exist outside the Golden Order's framework of value.
Demi-Humans are treated as animals by Golden Order society despite having their own organized communities and genuine queens who command real loyalty.
Malenia, the Blighted Bloom and her variants are beings of scarlet rot that have taken a plant-like, flower form, combining biological lushness with cosmic corruption.
The scarlet rot treats growth and decay as phases of a single process, collapsing the Golden Order's strict binary between life and death.
The Crucible Knights fighting in Crumbling Farum Azula are ancient Crucible entities that predate the Lands Between's current structure and even the Erdtree itself.
Crumbling Farum Azula exists outside normal time, which is interpreted as the reason these ancient Crucible beings have been preserved there intact.

Bell Bearing Hunters appear at night at the locations of wandering merchants, attacking anyone present and carrying bell bearings that let the player later buy the merchant's wares from an NPC after the hunters are defeated.
The appearance of Bell Bearing Hunters implies that something violent is happening to the merchants themselves, though the game never fully explains the connection.

The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC expands the game's bosses to explore what the Golden Order's divine structure was built upon, what it cost, and what persists in the hidden realm where those costs were paid.

Divine Beast Dancing Lion is a sacred construct rather than a natural animal, built to embody wild divine power using storm, snow, and thunder, reflecting the Land of Shadow's more reciprocal relationship with nature compared to the Golden Order.
Messmer, Mother of Fingers is revealed to be the original source of all Two Fingers and Three Fingers found throughout the Lands Between.
Messmer, Mother of Fingers is found broken in the Land of Shadow, her connection to the Greater Will severed or compromised.
Relena, Twin Moon Knight is found in Castle Ensis and wields both golden and cold moon magic, representing a tradition of moon sorcery that parallels Rennala's in a different context.
The nature of Relena's connection to Rennala (student, contemporary, relative, or otherwise) is never definitively established by the game.
Putrescent Knight guards the Cerulean Coast, defending a space of beauty that is already affected by rot and dissolution.
The Putrescent Knight's armor is encrusted with evidence of decay, showing it is partly consumed by the same dissolution process it was appointed to guard against, yet it continues its duty.
Commander Gaius rides an enormous armored boar through the Scadutree region and fights with tactical military precision, identifying the player simply as a problem within his patrol duties.
Gaius embodies institutional loyalty so complete that questioning the chain of command is not a cognitive option for him.
Romina, Saint of the Bud embodies rot as a form of growth and renewal rather than simple decay, with her arena filling with rot blooms as the fight progresses.
Romina is described as a saint who has achieved complete identification with the cosmic principle of rot she serves, such that the rot is not something she has but something she is.
The Scadutree Avatar is the Great Guardian of the Shadow Tree, the shadow counterpart to the Erdtree that grows in a realm alongside, not within, the Golden Order's world.
The Scadutree Avatar's guardianship predates the current age, dating to a time before the Erdtree dominated, when the Shadow Tree's realm was simply the world rather than a hidden counterpart.
Every boss in Elden Ring has an underlying story explaining why they are what they are and why they are found where they are, rather than being simple monsters.

Most bosses were engaged in their own ongoing existence before the player's arrival: Radahn was holding back the stars, Rennala was singing to her amber egg, Fortissax was fighting deathblight in the roots, the Fire Giant was chained to his forge, and Placidusax was waiting.
Elden Ring's bosses are framed as arguments the game makes about what power costs and what devotion produces, rather than mere obstacles.
Godrick represents the argument that borrowed power is still power, but remains borrowed.
Rennala represents the argument that grief is its own kind of kingdom.
Radagon represents the argument that a person can outlast everything that made them who they were.
Morgott represents the argument that one can love something that hates them, and that love can sustain without saving.
Malenia represents the argument that containing a god is its own form of power, and releasing it is honesty rather than defeat.
Power in the Lands Between is framed as the scar tissue of trauma: usually what remains after loss, what compensates for lack, or what was gained by surviving the unsurvivable.
The fog gate is interpreted as a threshold of attention, separating the ordinary world from a story the game has been saving, requiring commitment to enter and encounter it fully.

The Elden Ring itself is described as the fundamental law of the world given physical shape as a ring, with every boss existing in relationship to its breaking and the wars that followed the Shattering.
Godrick is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone too weak to compete for the largest fragments of the Elden Ring.
Rennala is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone whose connection to the Elden Ring was given to her rather than inherited.
Radahn is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone strong enough to fight for a fragment of the Elden Ring but too damaged to use it.
Morgott is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone who never held a fragment of the Elden Ring but devoted himself to the memory of its wholeness.
Malenia is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone whose fragment of the Elden Ring was always inside her, inseparable from her suffering.
The Tarnished is given purpose by the Shattering as someone with nothing left to lose, able to seek the truth of the Lands Between that no other being already present could uncover.
